ad_library.summary: 3 ad IDs opened directly on 2026-11-21, all active on the Roof Rays Solar Solutions page (page ID 61587695438410): 1825502928519547 (16 Nov, solar + EV), 1635924467937920 and 1184145723936677 (both 4 Nov, Rs.78,000 subsidy). An earlier read of the same page the same day showed 5 live ads, so treat the count as 3-5. All three click to a Facebook lead form rather than to roofrays.in. The site was read live the same day: four service lines, a four-step process, a Rs.1 lakh roof-protection assurance, a 5-year maintenance promise, a 14-27 working-day install window and a subsidy countdown dated 31 March 2027.

funnel.destination: Facebook lead form (FB.ME) - 'Get quote' on all 3 ads
funnel.meaning: Every live ad ends in a Facebook lead form, while the site carries a detailed qualification form (property type, residence type, housing-society name, average monthly bill) that would sort a homeowner from a housing society from a C&I buyer before anyone picks up the phone. None of this spend reaches that form, so the richest qualification data the business owns is not being used.

findings: All three live ads click to a Facebook lead form, never to roofrays.in - in a business that sells to homes, housing societies and commercial/industrial buyers separately, the site's own form (property type, residence type, society name, average monthly bill) would qualify each lead before the first call, and none of this spend reaches it.

The site's subsidy panel is a live countdown - 'Last date to apply 31 March 2027', '130 Days 02 Hrs 07 Mins' - while the ads never mention a deadline at all. The urgency asset exists and is not being used where the money is being spent.

The site promises 'Rs.1 Lakh Roof Protection Assurance' and '5-Year Expert Maintenance Support' and no live ad mentions either - the two most concrete, checkable offers the business has are missing from the creatives.

The site does publish an estimated price table and a units-to-kW guide - 3 kW Rs.1,45,000-2,10,000, 5 kW Rs.2,30,000-3,50,000, 10 kW Rs.4,80,000-7,20,000, and '300-450 units -> 3 kW' - on its residential guide page. None of the three ads carries a price or links to that page: the ads land on a lead form, so the one comparison asset the business owns is invisible to its paid traffic.

The ads target a Hyderabad homeowner with 'up to Rs.20,000 per month on fuel expenses' from a solar + EV combination, but no EV system, EV charger or worked EV example appears on the home page or the residential guide read for this report - the biggest number in the campaign is the one the destination does not set out.

The site publishes no customer name, review, install count, kW installed or project photograph with a locality anywhere, on a purchase that runs to lakhs and next to competitors quoting install counts in their first line.

The contact block gives the address as 'HUDA Complex, Tellapur' with no building, floor or plot number, while the Google Maps place it links to is pinned to a specific coordinate (17.4636, 78.2867) - a buyer checking the firm on a map gets a pin, not an address they can drive to.
next_steps: Point at least one ad at roofrays.in, not only at the lead form
The site already qualifies leads better than the Meta form does. Put a Meta Pixel and UTMs on it and send one creative there so the click becomes measurable and the qualification data survives.
Put the 31 March 2027 countdown into the ad copy

The site's own panel carries a live day counter. The same deadline, in the creative, is a stronger call to action than 'Get your FREE solar quotation' - and it is already the asset the business believes in.
Lead with the Rs.1 lakh roof-protection assurance

Roof damage and leakage is the single biggest objection in rooftop solar, and Roof Rays already sells a named assurance against it. It appears in no ad. Put it in the creative and on the landing page.
Point the ads at the price guide that already exists

The residential guide already answers the buyer's first question with a kW price range and a units-to-kW table. No ad links to it. Either send a creative there (with UTMs) or lift the 3 kW range into the ad itself so 'up to Rs.78,000' becomes a checkable number.
Either build an EV page or drop the Rs.20,000/month EV claim

The 16 Nov ad's entire hook is solar + EV savings, and no EV content was found on the pages read for this report. A short EV page with one worked example would make the claim verifiable; without it, the number is the weakest link in the campaign.
Publish the full street address and one local install
Add the building, floor and plot to the contact block, and one named Tellapur/Hyderabad install with a kW size. It converts a map pin into a business a buyer can check.

site_audit.platform: WordPress; single-page landing with a separate /connect-with-us/ contact page
site_audit.scope_note: The website was read live on 2026-11-21 through a rendered-content fetch of the home page. Tracking-pixel and head checks (Meta Pixel, GA4, GTM, Google Ads, meta description, Open Graph, JSON-LD, favicon) need the raw served HTML and were not captured through this channel, so they are recorded as not checked rather than absent. PageSpeed and sitemap were not run.

issues: No live chat — missing after-hours leads
No visible testimonials/social proof on homepage

site_evidence.note: Head HTML not captured through the sandbox fetch channel; pixel presence is not checked, not asserted absent. No UTM parameters appear on any link in the rendered page content, and the ads themselves land on an fb.me lead form, which carries no campaign parameters.

promise_gap.promise: 'Save up to Rs.20,000 per month on fuel expenses' (16 Nov ad)
promise_gap.site: No EV system, EV charger or worked EV example appears on the home page or the residential guide read for this report. The claim rests on 600 units a month from 5 kW, half of it surplus, which nothing read sets out.

promise_gap.promise: 'Up to Rs.78,000 in eligible government subsidy' (both 4 Nov ads)
promise_gap.site: The site states the subsidy deadline as 31 March 2027 and otherwise leaves the mechanics to the form - it does not say who applies, when it is credited, or what the buyer pays before it arrives.
The site gives the window but no ad does, and the FAQ does not say whether the clock starts at booking, at approval or at net-meter sanction - the part a buyer actually plans around.

ads_audit.methodology: Control review follows the claude-ads Meta Ads audit catalog (github.com/vamsy16/claude-ads, ads/references/meta-audit.md). Each control is graded only where public evidence establishes it - Ad Library ad data and the lead's own landing page. Controls that require Ads Manager access (bidding, budgets, audiences, learning phase, EMQ, CAPI status) are marked unknown on purpose: they cannot be verified from outside the account and are never guessed.
